defects.what: The contract fills the frame with rows of Japanese-looking kana/kanji pseudo-text and a red hanko-style seal; only the signature is needed.
The paper under the medallion is covered in Japanese pseudo-text with a red kanji banner at top left, and the medallion face itself carries glyph-like lettering.
The face looking at the medallion is a young shaggy-haired anime boy with no topknot, not Indio as drawn in the rest of the episode.
Newspaper stacks show large Japanese kana headlines (left and top right) plus columns of pseudo-text.
The party message on the phone screen begins with a line of Japanese text above the scribbled chat bubbles.
Every TV in the wall has a purple lower-third caption of katakana-like pseudo-text.
The protest placards carry scrawled pseudo-letters (not the script's 'magnanakaw, ibalik ang pera'), and the barrier tape has a row of fake lettering.
Both pages of the open Bible are packed with dense pseudo-text and a garbled header ('SVD NHLLA'), not the Proverbs 22:1 verse.
The deed of sale in front shows rows of CJK-like pseudo-text, a red seal and a blue stamp across the center of the frame.
The garage is shown as three stacked horizontal panels separated by hard seams, not one picture.
The impound scene is four stacked comic-strip panels, with an unrelated shaggy-haired figure cut into the bottom-left panel.
A split screen: two stacked garage panels on top and a separate close-up of three look-alike young men on the bottom.
A collage of six glowing picture cards (dog, girl with umbrella, two merged faces, trucks, coin) on a black letterboxed background.
A thick red rectangular border is drawn around the phone, like a frame inside the frame.
The dog in the foreground has two tall upright pointed ears and a Doberman-like head, so it does not read as Usman (one folded ear).
The dog at the bottom edge is tan/orange with two pointed ears, not black Usman.
The 1907 newspaper on the bench has CJK-like headline glyphs and faint columns of pseudo-text.
A wall chart on the right edge shows four large kanji-like characters.
A book spine at top right has two kanji characters on it.
The street reads as Tokyo: vertical shop signs and a marquee under the big screen show small kana-like lettering.
Bea's press ID shows two lines of fake lettering, and the mic has a small logo mark.
The mic flag has two network-style logos, and the press ID and lanyard show bits of pseudo-text.
JM's cap has a prominent circular logo emblem on the front.
Ma'am Celia appears inside a small phone-screen rectangle floating in a black void, which looks like a frame inside the frame.
The note card has a short scribble of pseudo-handwriting, not the script's line 'para sa mga gabing ganito'.
